collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a teen aged 14-17 and an adult)

collection.description: A teen learning to build wants to watch the builders of another village for a few days: give your blessing, or ask why.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been learning to build from (friend) for a year, and is good at it. But (subject.he/she) has heard that the builders in a village along the coast do things completely differently: curved roofs, no nails, walls that bend in a storm. (subject.He/she) wants to go and watch them for a few days. (subject.He/she) is worried (friend) will be hurt.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "What's wrong with how we build?" asks (friend). (subject) struggles to explain that nothing is wrong, (subject.he/she) just wants to see more. (friend) is quiet, then admits (friend.he/she) once wanted the same thing at that age and never went. "Go," (friend.he/she) says. "But come back and tell me everything." (subject) promises.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "Go," says (friend). "Come back and show me." (subject) goes. (subject.He/she) comes back with sketches scratched on bark and a lot of strong opinions about curved roofs. Some of the ideas are wonderful. Some don't work at all here. They argue about them happily for weeks, and both learn something.
